patch.value: GH-1671: linked tests have no setup step, so every command embeds its build and --add re-runs heavy suites just to fix metadata

GitHub issue #1671 (reported 2026-11-05 against 2026.11.4 from three fleet PR reviews: pm-vcs#182, pm-rl#145 and pm-linear#208). Linked test commands have no setup or prerequisite step. In TypeScript extension packages the specs import built output (../dist/index.js), so a linked command works only after npm run build, and every command must embed npm run build && itself (5 linked commands on pm-rl, each rebuilding). CodeRabbit flagged the missing build on all three PRs. Because pm test <id> --add verifies by running the command, a metadata-only fix re-runs every heavy suite (300-750 s each on pm-rl). Expected: a declared per-item or per-tracker setup step (for example pm test <id> --setup "npm run build" or a tests.setup settings key) that pm test --run executes once before the linked commands, recorded with provenance like the commands, cached by input digest where possible, and reported as a typed setup_failed result distinct from test failures. Also an explicit way to add a command without running it, recorded as verified false in provenance, so metadata fixes need no re-run. Why it matters for agents: linked tests are the evidence the next agent reproduces with pm test --run; a missing build today fails with a confusing module-not-found error, and the only workaround multiplies run time. Duplicate check: searched linked test setup, prerequisite, build step and pm test --run across all statuses. pm-dlvv (closed) added per-linked-test env directives, and pm-mf5z, pm-44iu and pm-wn34 (closed) enforce runnable command-required linked tests; none adds a setup phase or unverified add.

A per-item or per-tracker setup command can be declared through CLI, SDK and MCP, is stored with provenance, and pm test --run executes it once before the linked commands; A failing setup step is reported as a typed setup_failed result distinct from test failures, and no linked command runs after it; An explicit add-without-run option records the command with verified false in provenance, and pm test --run still executes it; Negative control: removing the setup execution makes a spec whose linked command needs the setup output fail

In a TypeScript extension package whose specs import ../dist/index.js: pm test <id> --add command='node --test test/x.test.js' on a clean checkout fails with module-not-found until the command embeds npm run build &&, and each --add re-runs the suite
A declared setup step runs once per pm test --run before linked commands, with provenance and a typed setup_failed result, and an explicit unverified add records verified false
pm test help lists only --shared-host-safe and --check-context; every linked command repeats the build and --add always executes the command

value.text:
Investigation note (2026-11-13), premise check for the add-without-run half: `pm test <id> --add` has never executed a command. On v2026.11.4 and on main, `runTest` only calls `executeSelectedLinkedTests` when `options.run === true`, and `--add` persists the entry inside `resolveLinkedTestItem` with `run_results: []`. A sandbox repro on the current build confirms it: `--add command="node t.js" --json` returned `run_results: []`. The misleading part was the help text. `--add` and `--add-json` read "Add verified isolated test", so the fleet ran `--add ... --run` to "verify", which re-runs every selected suite. A metadata-only fix already has a no-run path: `--update-index <n> --set-json '{...}'`.

Resolution of that half: the help now reads "Link isolated test; runs only with --run" for both flags, and docs/TESTING.md and docs/COMMANDS.md state that `--add` never executes and point to `--set-json` for metadata fixes. No `verified` provenance flag was added. Every `--add` is unverified, so the marker would be constant, and provenance is hashed into the trust fingerprint, so flipping it after a run would invalidate clone-local acknowledgements.

AC refinement (third clause): "an explicit add-without-run option records verified false" becomes "--add records a command without running it, help and docs say so, and pm test --run still executes it". The setup-phase clauses (1, 2 and 4) are implemented as specified.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Design (2026-11-13). The setup step is a per-item linked-test field, `phase: setup` (input `phase=setup|test`; `test`, the default, is stored as absent). It is not a tests.setup settings key: a settings-declared command is executable data that would bypass the provenance and clone-trust model every linked command goes through.

Behaviour:
- Ordering. `withLinkedTestSetupEntries` (src/sdk/test/run-phases.ts) prepends every stored setup entry to a selection that names at least one regular command. `selected_indexes` lists run order (setup positions first), and `setup_indexes` lists the setups the selector did not name. A selection of setups only runs just those. test-all uses `orderLinkedTestsSetupFirst` per item.
- Gate. `createLinkedTestSetupGate` runs inside `runLinkedTests`, which shares one sandbox, isolated root and snapshot across the item's entries, so setup output is visible to later entries. An executed setup that fails becomes `failure_category: setup_failed`, with the original class kept in `setup_failure_cause`. A refused setup keeps its category (trust_refusal or config_refusal), because its recovery differs. Either way every later entry gets a `skipped` row without executing. Setup rows carry `phase: setup` and are exempt from `--fail-on-empty-test-run` and `--require-assertions-for-pm`. They never satisfy `--measure`'s executed-test requirement (prerequisites.ts).
- test-all. Setups are excluded from the cross-item duplicate skip. A deduplicated setup leaves an isolated or snapshot sandbox without its output (the integration spec proves this with two items).
- Storage. `normalizeLinkedTest` keeps `phase`. `requiredItemFormatVersion` returns 3 when any test is a setup entry, and `CURRENT_ITEM_FORMAT_VERSION` is now 3, so hosts 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.13 refuse the item instead of silently dropping the field from its canonical hash. Create now stamps the required format as well (`stampCreatedItemFormat`). Before this change only edits stamped it, and create could not produce a guarded field until `phase`.
- Identity and trust. `phase` is not in `linkedTestsHaveSameIdentity`: the same command is not both a setup and a test of one item, so convert an entry with `--set-json`. It is not in the trust fingerprint either, because the command that executes is unchanged. Merge identity hashes the whole definition, so `phase` survives three-way merges.
- Line cap. execution.ts was at exactly 3400 effective lines. The failure-category type and counters moved to run-phases.ts and are re-exported, which leaves execution.ts at 3370.

Not done (follow-up): caching a passed setup across test-all items by input digest. The issue asked for it "where possible", and the AC does not require it.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Evidence, mixed-host check (2026-11-13). The published @unbrained/pm-cli@2026.11.13 was installed into an isolated npm prefix. npx is not valid for this check, because `npm install -g .` links the working tree under the same name@version, so npx runs the new build. Against a sandbox tracker whose item carries `phase: setup` at `pm_format_version: 3`:
- `get`, `update --priority 3` and `test --run` all refuse with "Stored item uses format version 3; this runtime supports up to 2. Upgrade pm before reading or changing". The item file is byte-identical afterwards.
- `list` still lists the item, because its light metadata read does not parse linked tests.
So an older host refuses the setup entry rather than silently dropping it.

Dogfooding decision: this PR adds no setup entry to this repository's own tracker items. Any pinned or bundled older SDK reading the tracker would refuse such an item until it upgrades; package consumers such as pm-changelog are one example. Adopt setup entries here only after the release that ships format 3 is the pinned floor.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Review round 1 on PR #1723 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh plus Greptile, 2026-11-13). Every finding was valid and is fixed in the follow-up commit.
1. (major, Codex and Greptile) In test-all, a setup refused before dispatch (an assignment-only command such as X=1, removed by resolveTestAllCommandRefusal) never reached the gate, so later commands ran. Fix: runTestAllItem drives a setup gate over its setup-first entries. A pre-dispatch setup refusal is recorded (phase setup, own category), and every later entry gets a blocked skip row without being dispatched.
2. (major, Codex) Cross-item regular-test dedupe ignored the item's setup. Two items with the same assertion command and different setups in isolated sandboxes ran it once. Fix: buildTestAllDedupeKey appends the item's setup signature (its setup keys), so a regular test is deduplicated only between items whose setups match.
3. (major, Greptile) A regular command reserved its dedupe key before its setup ran. When the first item's setup failed, a later item's identical command was skipped as a duplicate although it never executed. Fix: when any setup row of an item did not pass, the keys that item reserved are released.
4. (major, Codex and Greptile) A setup that never executed (a path-only entry promoted with --set-json, or a runtime safety skip) skipped every dependent behind ok: true. Fix: the gate turns a non-refused, non-passing setup into failed with setup_failed, so the run fails.
5. (major, Codex) The exported SDK runLinkedTests did not order setup entries itself. Fix: it runs orderLinkedTestsSetupFirst internally and returns results in run order. That is idempotent for pm test and test-all, which already pass setup-first lists.
6. (minor, Codex) Identical setups in test-all inherited the widest timeout across items. Fix: buildEffectiveTimeoutByKey skips setup entries, and keys regular tests by setup signature, so each setup runs with its own timeout.
Negative control: with the committed batch.ts restored, the three new test-all cases fail (refused-setup blocking, setup-aware dedupe with key release, timeout keying).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: When a new execution phase gates later entries, every path that can produce a row for an entry must pass through the same gate: the in-sandbox loop, pre-dispatch refusals, and any batch-level dedupe or skip. A row made outside the gate silently bypasses the dependency it declares. Batch-level caches keyed by a command (dedupe keys, effective timeouts) must also include what the command depends on (its item's setup signature). They should reserve a key only once the command really executes, or release the reservation when a prerequisite blocks it.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text:
Review round 2 on PR #1723 (Codex gpt-6.1-sol xhigh on 9182dbdf1, 2026-11-13). Codex verified the round-1 fixes and found two more test-all defects, both valid and fixed.
1. (major) The setup signature reused buildLinkedTestKey, which collapses whitespace inside quoted strings. Two isolated items whose setups wrote 'a  b' and 'a b' shared a signature, so the second item's failing test was skipped as a duplicate. Fix: resolveSetupSignature is now a stableStringify of each setup's executable definition, which keeps command bytes verbatim. Provenance, editor stamps, note and timeout are left out: they do not change what a setup produces, and a setup that times out releases its keys.
2. (minor) A refusal planned for a later entry (an assignment-only X=1) was reported as config_refusal even when an earlier setup had failed at run time, so it counted as a second failure. Fix: result assembly replays the executed setup outcomes through a run-time gate. A planned refusal after a failed setup becomes the blocked skip, and entries the sandbox already skipped get the same blocked row. The gate now records an already-typed setup_failed row unchanged, so it is idempotent on replay.
Specs: the whitespace-signature keys in the timeout-keying case, plus a new runtime-failure-then-planned-refusal case in tests/integration/linked-tests/linked-test-setup-phase.integration.spec.ts.
